en: The Heart of Śrī Rāma
Salutations to Śrī Gaṇeśa.
Śrī Mahādeva said:
Then Rāma himself spoke to Hanumān, who stood before him:
"Listen to that which I shall declare concerning the self, the non-self, and the supreme Self."
Just as a great threefold division of space is observed:
the vast space within a body of water, the space delimited by it, and another, called the reflected space; thus the sky appears in three ways. || 2 ||
Consciousness delimited by the intellect is one; the full [unconditioned] is another;
and the reflection is yet another which serves as the prototype—thus consciousness is threefold. (3)

The agency of the intellect, which is accompanied by appearances, is erroneously superimposed through delusion upon the undivided and changeless Witness; likewise, the state of being a living individual (jīvatva) is so attributed by the ignorant.
The appearance, however, is a false cognition and is said to be the effect of ignorance;
that Brahman is indeed uninterrupted, whereas the sense of separation is merely conceptualized.
Through the sentence "That thou art" and others, the uninterrupted [consciousness] attains oneness with the Full,
as does the "I" together with its appearance.
When the knowledge of the oneness of the two selves has arisen through the Great Sentence (mahāvākya), then ignorance, along with its effects, is destroyed; of this there is no doubt.

Having understood this, my devotee attains my own state of being; for those who are averse to devotion to me and are deluded within the pits of the scriptures, there can be neither knowledge nor liberation even in hundreds of births.
O sinless one, this secret, the very heart of my own self, has been spoken by me directly to you;
it must not be given by you to one devoid of devotion to me or to a rogue, even in exchange for a kingdom greater than that of Indra.
In the glorious Adhyātmarāmāyaṇa, in the Bālakāṇḍa, the Śrīrāmahṛdaya is complete.
Salutations to Śrī Gaṇeśa.
Śrī Mahādeva said:
Then Rāma himself spoke to Hanumān, who had approached him.
Listen to that which I shall proclaim concerning the self, the non-self, and the supreme self.
Just as a great threefold division of space is observed:
the great space within a body of water, the space limited by that very [water], and another, called the reflected space; thus the sky is seen to be threefold. (2)
Consciousness delimited by the intellect is one; the full [unconditioned] is another;
and the reflection, which is the very prototype, is the third—thus consciousness is threefold.

The agency of the intellect, along with its appearances, is erroneously superimposed through delusion upon the undivided, unchanging Witness; likewise, the state of being a living soul (jīvatva) is so attributed by the ignorant.
The appearance, however, is a false cognition and is said to be the effect of ignorance;
that Brahman is indeed uninterrupted, whereas the sense of separation is merely conceptualized.
The uninterrupted [consciousness] attains oneness with the Full through such statements as "That thou art," and likewise the "I" together with its appearance.
When the knowledge of the oneness of the two selves arises through the Great Saying (mahāvākya), then ignorance, along with its effects, is surely destroyed; of this there is no doubt.
Having understood this, my devotee attains my own state of being;
for those who are averse to devotion to me and are deluded within the pits of the scriptures,
there shall be neither knowledge nor liberation even in hundreds of births.
O sinless one, this secret heart of my own self has been spoken by me directly to you;
it must not be given by you to one devoid of devotion to me or to a rogue, even if they offer a kingdom greater than that of Indra.
Thus concludes the Śrī Rāma-hṛdaya in the Bālakāṇḍa of the glorious Adhyātma-Rāmāyaṇa.
